item.title: F1 makes final call on Qatar and Abu Dhabi amid Middle East situation
item.description: Formula 1 has confirmed that end-of-season races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead as scheduled. The final two rounds of the 2026 season in Qatar (29 November) and Abu Dhabi (6 December) had been shrouded in uncertainty due to the conflict in the Middle East . Races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia earlier this season were cancelled , though Bahrain did fulfil its event with a one-off race in Malaysia in October. F1 did have the historic Imola circuit as a back-up contingency plan for 6 December, with preliminary grandstand work underway in and around the track site in the Emilia Romagna region of Italy. However, given logistical and freight plans, The Independent understands that F1 has now told Imola to stand down. Qatar and Abu Dhabi will conclude the campaign as planned as part of one final triple-header, starting in Las Vegas on 21 November. An F1 spokesperson added: “We are very grateful for the support and collaboration with the promoter and government in Imola and the region. If the situation develops negatively in the coming weeks before the events in the Middle East we will not hesitate to do the right thing and the safety of everyone will always be the priority.” F1 added that all 11 teams are supportive of concluding the season as planned. The final round of the MotoGP season took place in Qatar – at the same circuit in Lusail, just outside Doha – over the weekend without a hitch, though Yamaha did withdraw from the event pre-race. Nineteen riders also penned a letter expressing their wish not to race in Qatar, but both races were held as planned. Previous UK travel guidance during the height of the US/Israel-Iran conflict this year advised against “all but essential” travel to Qatar and Abu Dhabi. However, that has since been lifted, with tension in the region cooling in recent weeks. That being said, the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) does state that the “broader security context” in the Middle East “carries a risk of sudden escalation, potential flight cancellations and airspace disruptions.” Both F1 chief Stefano Domenicali and FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem have insisted in recent weeks that the Middle Eastern races will take place as planned, barring any sudden re-escalation of hostilities in the region. item.title: “Doesn’t Hurt That You Have $50M+”: Kyle Whittingham Shifts Attention to Oregon’s Massive Recruiting Budget Ahead of Ducks Clash
item.description: Michigan football head coach Kyle Whittingham speaks as he is being introduced on the floor during the first half between Michigan and USC at Crisler Center © Imagn Michigan football is at a crossroads as it aims to rescue its college football season, and the pressure is on Kyle Whittingham. The Wolverines’ head coach made the decision to fire offensive coordinator Jason Beck after an unsatisfactory run of performances, but he still needs to win games to keep his own job secure. Ahead of the game against the Oregon Ducks, who are themselves turning a corner after some tough results, Whittingham shifted attention to Oregon’s massive recruiting budget, highlighting the difference between the two sides. “He really does a great job recruiting and it doesn’t hurt that you have $50+ million dollars at your disposal to, in essence outbid everybody. Not everybody, but a lot of people. But that’s not his fault,” Whittingham said about head coach Dan Lanning to reporters, via Inside Michigan . He further said that he meant it as a credit to the program and its desire to focus on young athletes in the NIL era. “That’s a credit. I mean, that’s a credit to their program and their dedication and desire to win and the support they have. NIL is the name of the game in recruiting these days. It’s shifted so much,” he went on. Kyle Whittingham Explained Why He Fired Jason Beck After a tough defeat to Michigan State, offensive coordinator Jason Beck received his marching orders from Kyle Whittingham, and he addressed the decision to media personnel. “Well, watching the film really was the deciding factor, and I had the intention of waiting until after the season, as I mentioned,” Whittingham said to reporters, as reported by Wolverines Wire . He further revealed when it became completely clear to him that a change was needed. “But when I turned the film on and really dove into it, it just became apparent to me that you need to make the change now. And there’s just too much regression in the offense in that particular game. And that’s what led to the decision.” Whittingham also confirmed no other person was involved in making the decision but himself. The decision will be put to the test as the Wolverines play the Oregon Ducks on Saturday. item.title: Greyson Fuller's 1,000-yard season is only a first step to become South's next great QB
item.description: EAST STROUDSBURG – Is Greyson Fuller the next great East Stroudsburg South quarterback? The jury is still out, but the junior signal-caller took the first step towards earning that distinction. Fuller, who completed his first season as the full-time starter for the Cavaliers after stepping up as a sophomore in 2025, became the 17 th South QB to throw for at least 1,000 yards in a single season, finishing the 2026 campaign with 1,767 yards. He nearly reached this milestone last season after filling in for an injured Ivan Laubach, but now the milestone is officially his. “It feels great,” Fuller said about the accomplishment. “I grew up looking at the banner hanging in the gym of all the 1,000-yard guys, and it’s going to be awesome seeing my name up there.” Going to the 'ship: East football avenges Bucket Game loss, beats PV to advance to 5A district title game South head coach Matt Walters has consistently commended Fuller’s development from his sophomore year to his junior year, and he’s proud of how he reached the milestone. As great as the milestone is, however, it’s only a first step on the path to be among the program greats. Granted, Fuller’s 1,767 yards rank him seventh all-time in program history for single-season passing yards, and 15 th all-time amongst all Pocono quarterbacks. But here are the fellow Cavaliers ahead of him: Jake Cirillo, who threw for 1,000 yards all four years of high school before going to play for East Stroudsburg University Ivan Laubach, a 2,000-yard passer who led South to a district championship. Bobby McClosky, an EPC North MVP, and a First Team All-State Selection And Rob Moyer, the area’s all-time leader in single-season passing yards, and the only player in Pocono history to pass for 2,000 yards twice Even some of the names behind Fuller who lack in numbers make up for the difference in accolades. ESU head coach Jimmy Terwilliger was the first East Stroudsburg (before the split) quarterback to have multiple 1,000-yard seasons, and he did that with a coach who ran the option in the legend Ed Christian. Oh yeah, and he later earned the honor of the best player in Division II football. And there’s also Will Fish, who joined the 1,000-yard club in 2019 and nearly threw for 2,000 his junior year and went on to play at Lycoming College. Fish is now on staff at South, where he watched Fuller throw for 303 passing yards and five touchdowns against Pocono Mountain West. “Coach Fish talked to me on the sidelines midgame and asked me how many touchdowns I was at,” Fuller said. “He then said, ‘All right, my record is six touchdowns. item.title: Managerial 'inconsistency' hurting Ghana - Hughton
item.description: Kim Bjorkegren (right) is in interim charge of Ghana after Carlos Queiroz left the Black Stars by mutual consent [Getty Images] As Ghana prepare for two make-or-break 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifiers with women's coach Kim Bjorkegren in temporary charge, former boss Chris Hughton has called for greater consistency in the Black Stars dugout. The West Africans face Somalia in back-to-back fixtures over the next week, having lost their first two games in Group C against Ivory Coast and The Gambia last month. Those defeats resulted in the departure of Carlos Queiroz, whose brief period in the hot seat was characterised by uncertainty. The Portuguese's exit means Swede Bjorkegren, who has been in charge of the Black Queens since January 2025, has now been asked to lead the men's team against Somalia. "When you have inconsistency in the amount of time when a manager is staying, it's never good," Hughton told BBC Sport Africa. "You want that consistency in the players [and] the players want that consistency in what they see in the manager." Queiroz, who had two spells as Sir Alex Ferguson's assistant at Manchester United, was initially appointed in April and led Ghana to the last 32 of the Fifa World Cup, holding England to a goalless draw in the group stage, before announcing his own departure shortly after the team were eliminated 1-0 by Colombia in the last 32. However, the 73-year-old was reappointed in early September, with the Ghana Football Association (GFA) praising his "extensive international experience" gained during time in charge of South Africa, Egypt, Portugal, Iran, Colombia, Qatar and Oman. But Queiroz's return lasted less than a month following a 2-0 defeat by the Ivorians in Bouake and a 4-2 humbling against the Gambians in front of home fans in Accra. "What I saw in the World Cup is that they represented the country very well, particularly the England game," said Hughton. "And although it was very much a defensive outfit, there were opportunities to score." Hughton, however, admits that regular sackings can create an "attitude" within a squad, with players knowing that "if he (the coach) doesn't do well then he won't be there". item.title: Vikings vs. Packers odds: Vikings underdogs heading into Lambeau
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Christian Benford #47 of the Buffalo Bills breaks up a pass intended for Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings during the first quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images After falling out of first place in the NFC North for the first time this season, the Minnesota Vikings will look to avoid moving into the division’s basement when they head to Lambeau Field in Week 10 to conclude their home-and-home series with the Green Bay Packers for this season. The people who set the betting lines, apparently, don’t like their chances. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the lines for Sunday’s game, and the Vikings currently sit as a 4.5-point underdog to the Packers. The over/under for the game currently rests at 42.5 points. The Vikings, as we all saw on Monday Night Football, appear to have completely abandoned the concept of offense, as they generated none of it in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills for their second loss in a row. Carson Wentz stepped in at quarterback for the injured Kyler Murray and turned in what may have been the worst start a Vikings quarterback has put together in recent memory, completing just 8-of-25 passes and turning the ball over three times, including two interceptions. . .a number that could have been significantly higher. The Packers, on the other hand, have won five of their last six after getting off to a 1-2 start. This past week, they absolutely thumped the New England Patriots to the tune of 45-27 behind three more touchdown passes from Jordan Love and a defense that forced Drake Maye into three interceptions. The Packers currently sit in last place in the North, but with a 6-3 record would lead either the NFC South or the NFC East. . .that’s just how good the NFC North has been this season. These two teams met in the regular season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz came into the game midway through the first quarter after Murray suffered a concussion, and the Packers had a 22-10 lead with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter. From there, however, the Minnesota defense took over, leading an onslaught against Love and the Green Bay offense that saw the Vikings score 29 unanswered points to finish the game, including forcing a turnover on downs and generating an interception and a fumble to set up scoring opportunities. Minnesota took home the 39-22 win to get their season off to a 1-0 start. With the NFL trade deadline looming at 3:00 PM Central today. . .or approximately seven hours from when this story goes up. . .we will see if anything the Vikings do (or don’t do) will shift this number at all. As it stands now, however, the Vikings are currently an underdog to their division rivals as the second half of the season officially gets underway.

item.title: FIA boss looks to ‘end age limits’ for office holders – six months after ditching term limits
item.description: Mohammed Ben Sulayem is reportedly looking to end age limits for FIA office holders – just six months after the FIA president ditched term limits for those in leadership posts. Emirati executive Ben Sulayem, 64, has been FIA president since December 2021 and was re-elected last year after other candidates were prevented from standing, due to quirks in the FIA statutes which meant the only prospective vice-president in one region was already aligned with Ben Sulayem. Currently, FIA statutes rule out anyone over the age of 75 from standing for a presidential term. This rule was implemented in 2024 to “modernise the governance of the FIA and ensure that candidates for the presidency are more aligned with current leadership practices.” Yet just six months after Ben Sulayem ended term limits for those in leadership posts, the BBC reports that Ben Sulayem wants to discontinue the age-limit rule and put forward a proposal detailing as such to the FIA’s General Assembly in Shanghai next month. An FIA spokesperson told The Independent: “An age limit excludes candidates solely on the basis of their date of birth, regardless of their experience, expertise, or ability to contribute. Ultimately, the competent FIA bodies will retain full authority to elect the officeholders they deem appropriate.” “The proposal to remove age limits for FIA officeholders is one of the proposed amendments to the FIA Statutes to be put to the General Assembly in Shanghai in December. It was approved by the World Councils for submission in line with the process set out in the FIA Statutes, and will only take effect if the General Assembly votes in favour.” Ben Sulayem had originally introduced an upper age limit of 70 in 2023, in a move widely seen to prevent Motorsport UK boss David Richards from running. Ben Sulayem, who is a regular in parc ferme and on the podium after F1 races, has overseen controversial moments in his near-five years in charge. Ben Sulayem has clashed with Max Verstappen in the past (Getty) His first term saw Ben Sulayem clash with Lewis Hamilton over the Brit’s desire to wear jewellery in the cockpit, while he also angered drivers, including four-time world champion Max Verstappen, for issuing fines for swearing. Last April, Robert Reid resigned as deputy president for sport, accusing the governing body of a "breakdown in governance standards." And presidential candidates such as Tim Mayer and Laura Villars were unhappy after they could not oppose him in last year’s presidential elections. FIA rules dictate a vice-president candidate must be nominated from each of its six global regions; Bernie Ecclestone’s wife, Fabiana, the sole South American candidate, supported Ben Sulayem. Meanwhile, Ben Sulayem has also voiced his support for end-of-season races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi to go ahead. A final call is expected on Tuesday.

item.title: Former Royals catcher and manager Bob Boone dies at age 78
item.description: BOSTON, MA - MAY 22: Bob Boone #8 of the Kansas City Royals takes a swing during a baseball game against the Boston Red Sox on May 22, 1989 at Fenway Park in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bob Boone, a four-time All-Star catcher who spent two seasons as a player with the Kansas City Royals before managing the club for parts of three seasons, has died at the age of 78, according to a social media post from his family . The son of All-Star infielder Ray Boone, and the father of All-Star infielders Bret and Aaron Boone, the Boones were the first family to have three generations of MLB players. RIP Bob Boone, the great Gold Glove, All Star and World Series champion catcher, who passes away at 78. Condolences to wife Sue and sons Aaron and Bret Boone. What a marvelous man and privilege and honor to know. — Bob Nightengale (@BNightengale) November 10, 2026 Bob Boone was one of the most accomplished defensive catchers of his generation, winning seven Gold Glove Awards over a 19-year playing career. He was originally drafted by the Philadelphia Phillies after a standout career at Stanford. He he finished third in Rookie of the Year voting and was a three-time All-Star with the Phillies. He faced the Royals in the 1980 World Series as a catcher for the Phillies, hitting .412 (7-for-17) in the series for his only championship. He moved onto the Angels in 1982, helping them win the division in their first year, earning MVP votes, and winning a Gold Glove. He was an All-Star the next year, and over seven years in Anaheim, he set the club record for most games behind the plate. He left Anaheim and signed with the Royals in 1989 at the age of 41. He appeared in 131 games and hit .274/.351/.323, winning his seventh Gold Glove and finishing with 2.4 rWAR. After 40 games in 1990, he retired. After the 1994 season was cancelled during the work stoppage, the Royals hired Bob Boone as manager to replace Hal McRae and usher in a new youth movement. Despite trading away stars like David Cone and Brian McRae, the Royals were in the hunt for the new “Wild Card” spot for most of the season, until a poor September caused them to fall under .500 at 70-74. Boone was a very cerebral manager, but would frequently clash with the media. He was criticized for constantly changing the lineup, and for employing “Boonieball,” as then-Kansas City Star columnist Jeffrey Flanagan would call his style of play. Boone finished just 75-86 in 1996, and was fired at the 1997 All-Star break after a 36-46 start, replaced by Tony Muser. Boone would later manage the Cincinnati Reds from 2001-2003, although he never managed them to a winning season. He joined the Washington Nationals front office in 2005 and served the team until he retired in 2021.

item.title: USMNT could lose head coach just months after signing extension
item.description: Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - United States Press Conference - Los Angeles Stadium, Inglewood, California, U.S. - June 11, 2026 U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino during the press conference REUTERS/Daniel Cole Manchester United have gotten off to the worst start in their Premier League history, and it looks like Michael Carrick is about to pay the price. The club is reportedly ready to fire its manager, with United sitting in the relegation zone after just one win in 10 league games. And United’s top choice to replace him could come as a big blow to American soccer fans. U.S. men’s national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly the favorite for the job, less than four months after signing a contract extension with U.S. Soccer. Pochettino and the USMNT Pochettino took over the USMNT in 2024 with the goal of leading the team on a deep run in the World Cup on home soil. Instead, the U.S. was eliminated in the Round of 16 by Belgium in a blowout loss. That run also came with its share of controversy. Pochettino later admitted it was a “mistake” after FIFA overturned a suspension to Folarin Balogun ahead of the Belgium match, a decision that came after President Donald Trump said he had contacted FIFA president Gianni Infantino about it. He also didn’t mince words about Christian Pulisic’s struggles. Still, U.S. Soccer stood by Pochettino after the tournament, and in August, it announced that he had signed a new deal that runs through the 2030 World Cup. Manchester United’s Interest According to ESPN’s Mark Ogden and Rob Dawson , United’s leadership, including co-chairman Joel Glazer and minority owner Jim Ratcliffe, has been assessing Carrick’s future. Sources told ESPN that there is “now acceptance that performances and results demand a change of manager.” Carrick took over as interim manager in January and led United to Champions League qualification, earning a two-year contract this summer. But the club has won just one of four games since giving him time to turn things around last month, leaving United one point off the bottom of the table. Pochettino, who has interviewed for the United job three times before, is regarded as having “the Premier League experience and personality needed to drag United out of danger,” per the report. The former Tottenham, Chelsea, and PSG manager also reportedly has a $10 million escape clause in his U.S. Soccer contract, which United would have to pay. Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, and Kieran McKenna are also reportedly among the candidates. United’s next match is against Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22. Needless to say, U.S. Soccer will be watching this one closely. item.description: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Quinn, a one-year-old corgi weighing just 25 pounds, broke free from her handlers during halftime at Bank of America Stadium on Sunday. The small dog dodged several attempts to catch her before finally being corralled near the 40-yard line, according to wtvcfox. While the Denver Broncos secured a 26-21 victory over the Carolina Panthers, the real highlight of the game belonged to the short-legged pup who turned a planned race into a chaotic dash. Although HITC reports that Ollie won the race, Quinn stole the show by dashing around the field after the event. Quinn appeared destined for the end zone before handlers managed to bring her under control. The hilarious video of the escape made the NFL Red Zone channel, spreading the moment far beyond the stadium. Beforehand, even the Panthers players got involved by offering their predictions for the race. Durden told WRAL that they take Quinn out to a field every day and make her run, and she would run straight into Gilgan’s arms. Even Durden struggled to catch Quinn on the football field during practice. The dog’s real name is Quinn, though she was referred to as ‘Lennox’ throughout social media memes after Barstool Sports shared a graphic with that wrong name, per HITC. The Charlotte Corgi Club, which organized the event, confirmed her name in a statement. “Go Quinn Go! We had the best time at the Carolina Panthers game today and always love being a part of halftime!” the group said on their Facebook page, according to HITC. A Community Effort on the Field Getting a spot in the race is not guaranteed for every dog owner. Julie Sippy, who founded the Charlotte Corgi Club, told WRAL that corgi owners contribute $15 to a raffle with the goal of obtaining one of the 12 available positions for the halftime race. This year, 137 corgi parents submitted tickets for the chance to be on the field. Proceeds from the event were divided equally between the club and that year’s charity organization. item.title: ‘No One Wants This’: NCAAF Playoff Expands To 24 Teams, Kills SEC Title Game
item.description: Georgia quarterback Stetson Bennett (13) raises the SEC Championship MVP trophy after the SEC Championship NCAA college football game between LSU and Georgia in Atlanta, on Saturday, Dec. 3, 2022. Georgia won 50-30. News Joshua L Jones Starting in 2027, the College Football Playoff will expand to 24 teams, while the SEC Championship Game will be eliminated. ESPN and the playoff committee finalized a five-year deal valued at nearly $1.7 billion , triggering this huge change. ESPN is set to pay an additional $345 million per year for this new larger format. On Nov. 9, the College Football Playoff Management Committee unanimously approved expansion to 24 teams beginning with the 2027–28 season. The CFP also announced a new media-rights agreement with ESPN, which will carry the expanded playoff through the 2031–32 season. Fans do not appear excited about the changes, as CFP executive director Rich Clark noted earlier this week , “We’re aware of the fan sentiment and that many fans aren’t in favor of expansion. It was considered, but ultimately, we just need to make a spectacular playoff.” Regular Season Games Still Count Some people worry that a bigger bracket means the regular season loses its sting. Earlier this season, Will Stein, the head coach at Kentucky, even spoke about the idea that regular season games might no longer matter. “I think that’s a really lame take, to be honest,” he said Tuesday at his weekly news conference . “As far as I know, every game in college football is still going to matter. … So (the playoff) definitely needed to expand.” Stein made it clear that fans should not dismiss the importance of every Saturday. item.title: World Cup finalists England still feel short of best
item.description: Rob Hawkins laughed when asked by BBC Sport whether he had been practising his dives. The question was prompted by some spectacular athleticism as he scored five tries to help England crush Australia 86-18 in Tuesday's Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup semi-final in Wollongong, Australia. "It's just off-the-cuff stuff when needed," he said. "Some of the kicks were cautious!" The man who had provided many of those kicks, Nathan Collins, was sitting beside him. He did not disagree. "He makes my bad kicks look good!" Collins said. "It is great to have him there to sweep up. He's great to play with and against." England have reason to be in good spirits as they prepare for a fifth successive World Cup final, the fourth in a row against great rivals France. They are looking to defend the title they won on home ground four years ago, a narrow 28-24 victory in Manchester . All of the three previous finals between the two teams have been tight: France won 42-40 in Gillingham in 2013, and 38-34 in Perpignan in 2017. England seemed to set themselves up perfectly for Friday's final, scoring 15 tries against Australia. Hawkins' five scores, plus five conversions, took his personal points tally to 30 points. His best try, and the standout from the whole game, was the third one - a long-range punt from England seemed to be a shot to nothing, but not where Hawkins was concerned. He chased it down and, millimetres away from the dead-ball line, managed to grab the ball and get it down under huge pressure from Adam Tannock, who he had outpaced. Yet Hawkins thought his and England's performances were far from perfect. "Wouldn't say we are 10 out of 10 yet, there are still good a good few things to look at," he said. "Today was a six or seven. Hopefully the best is to come on Friday. "Today was satisfying but not easy. We had the crowd to fight and a ruthless Australian team. But we are happy with the result." England will now reset for their latest showdown with France, which will kick off at 08:45 GMT on Friday at WIN Entertainment Centre. item.title: Frank Kennedy’s Q School DQ Sparks Debate On Green Damage
item.description: Stephen Lew-USA TODAY Sports Frank Kennedy, a 21-year-old English pro, found out the hard way on Monday that the DP World Tour will not tolerate damage to the putting surface. After allegedly removing a one-foot divot from the 11th green at Infinitum Golf in Spain, officials disqualified him from the Final Stage of Qualifying School. Kennedy claims the damage was not intentional. He told the world on Instagram that he missed a birdie putt and swung his club in frustration, noting that the putter “accidentally caught the surface.” He insists he did not mean to hurt the green and that his playing partner helped fix it right away. “I am hugely disappointed to have been disqualified …” Kennedy wrote, according to a report . He added that reports claiming he damaged the course on purpose are “wholly incorrect.” The young golfer admitted he should have called a referee to check the repair before moving on, but he argues that accidental contact should not cost him his entire tournament. The Rules Do Not Care About Feelings While Kennedy says he learned a lesson, the rules of golf are strict about who fixes what and when. The DP World Tour confirmed to Monday Q Info that the disqualification was necessary because the damage was deemed deliberate. The top 15 players and ties will earn DPWT cards for 2027, a prize Kennedy now misses. If players can damage greens and claim it was an accident without consequence, the rules become meaningless. The tournament officials saw a player swing a club and hit the green, causing a visible divot. They decided that the act was egregious enough to end his run. Kennedy stated he would respect the outcome of a review, but the initial ruling stands firm. Accidents Happen, But Consequences Remain Kennedy shot a 69 in the fourth round and was in position to make the cut before the DQ. Even if the damage was not meant to be malicious, the result was the same: a ruined putting surface and a disqualified player. After posting a 69 in the fourth round, Kennedy tied for the final spot in the top 60 to play the last two rounds. His DQ shifted the cut line from 12 under to 11 under, causing seven players who would have been eliminated to survive instead. DPWT cards for 2027 will be awarded to the top 15 players and ties.

item.title: Barcelona star De Jong open to Netherlands captaincy: ‘It would be an honour’
item.description: Barcelona star De Jong open to Netherlands captaincy: ‘It would be an honour’ After an injury-laden summer, Frenkie de Jong will once again return to Dutch colours this week as we enter the second international break of the season. The Barcelona midfielder is coming on the back of a stellar cameo against Atletico Madrid, where he was able to calm the game and help his team secure a 2-1 victory. Now back in the Netherlands camp under the new but familiar manager, Xavi Hernandez, Frenkie is tipped to become the team captain in the absence of Virgil van Dijk. Frenkie open to captaincy De Jong addressed the media over the possibility of becoming a captain, confirming that the final decision is up to Xavi. De Jong played a key role in Barcelona’s win over Atletico Madrid. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) But the Barcelona midfielder stated he would be more than happy to become the captain of the national team, in the absence of van Dijk. “It depends on the coach to announce it, but it is certainly possible. I’m not very talkative. Virgil is always heard above others, he is our true leader, also verbally. “When I wear the armband, I can set an example for others with my behaviour and professionalism,” he said (h/t SPORT ). De Jong added that his captaincy style could be a mix of both Lionel Messi and van Dijk, as he is not really a vocal leader on the pitch. “I also experienced having Messi as captain. He never raised his voice and was the undisputed boss. Let’s say that, with the armband, I would be somewhere between Messi and Virgil. It would be a great honour if it happened this week ,” he added. De Jong on Xavi’s methods Frenkie has worked with Xavi in the past. (Photo by Catherine Ivill/Getty Images) De Jong went on to talk about Xavi’s adaptation and tactical setup in the Netherlands team, having previously worked with the Spaniard at Barcelona. “It is very clear in their approach and what they want to see. During the first international break I already observed some patterns in the construction of the game that are characteristic of it. The fact that I was also a midfielder is especially pleasant .” The Barcelona midfielder is also open to the possibility of appearing alongside Borussia Dortmund Joey Veerman. “I agree with the coach in which good footballers can always play together. Joey is tactically solid, technically good and has a great vision of play. There are a lot of midfielders in the national team that I can play with ,” he said. Finally, the Dutchman offered an update on his fitness, having recently returned from a long injury layoff. “I’m fit, happy and very motivated. I don’t think you’ll learn anything from injuries, but you do want to play football again ,” he concluded.

He has demonstrated real leadership qualities at a young age. That booking he received for what I considered an outstanding tackle against Chelsea galvanized the crowd and the entire Everton squad — he was stepping up and taking responsibility. Harrison has the tools in his arsenal, and with each additional game comes greater experience, greater knowledge, and continued development. You absorb lessons from the best players around you in the locker room and incorporate that into your own game. This is a tremendous moment for the academy. We've endured years of frustration watching talented players denied their shot, and in some cases, we've allowed them to leave. Seeing one of our brightest prospects finally given his opportunity — and seizing it — is exactly what this club needed.
